key_insight: HaRP uses two complementary shutter-scanning views, RSGR and inverted RSGR, to recover high dynamic range photosequences while reducing rolling-shutter motion artifacts. The core idea is to turn the sensor’s scanning direction into a source of richer information rather than a limitation.
problem_solved: Standard CMOS mobile cameras suffer from rolling-shutter distortion, and even RSGR mode trades away capture speed and dynamic range. This paper addresses the need for a faster way to capture motion scenes with fewer geometric artifacts and better exposure coverage.
method: Introduce a dual reversed scanning setup that captures both RSGR and inverted RSGR views of the scene.
Fuse the complementary scan directions to reconstruct high dynamic range photosequences.
Leverage the two-view capture geometry to mitigate rolling-shutter distortions and preserve motion details.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical camera-side solution that improves the quality of training and inference data for dynamic scenes. It can benefit mobile imaging, computational photography, and downstream vision tasks that rely on cleaner motion-rich inputs.
